The hook is `useSession()`. It reads a global session store that `current-user.ts` keeps up to date, and it never returns `null`. When nobody is logged in, the session comes back with `authenticated: false` instead of being absent. The one exception is a backend that fails before any session has loaded, which the hook can't resolve to a session at all.

**How a component reads the session**

- `useSession()` returns a `Session` object and suspends (throws a promise) until the first session has loaded. It then subscribes to the store so the component re-renders on login, logout, or user-property changes. (`openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-react-utils/src/useSession.ts:17-116`)
- The store is a global store created in `current-user.ts`. `getSessionStore()` triggers a refresh if the data is stale and returns the store. (`openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-api/src/current-user.ts:29-32`, `:164-167`)
- `refetchCurrentUser()` requests the session endpoint and passes the result to `handleSessionResponse()`. (`openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-api/src/current-user.ts:251-277`, `:567-602`)
- `getCurrentUser()` is the promise-based alternative for non-React code. (`openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-api/src/current-user.ts:105-120`)
- `setUserLanguage()` runs on every loaded session and sets `<html lang>` from the user's locale. (`openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-api/src/current-user.ts:195-215`)

**What happens when nobody is authenticated**

- A 401 or 403 from the session endpoint is treated as "not logged in", not as a failed lookup. If the response body is an unauthenticated session, the store stores that body. Otherwise the store is cleared to `{ loaded: true, session: { authenticated: false, sessionId: '' } }`. (`openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-api/src/current-user.ts:580-590`, `:604-606`, `:634-636`, `:291-299`)
- In that case the hook returns a session with `authenticated === false`, so components check that flag rather than looking for null.
- Separately, `openmrs-fetch.ts` redirects the browser on a 403 from the session endpoint, or on any status listed in `redirectAuthFailure.errors`. The target is the configured URL, then the response's `location` header, then `${openmrsSpaBase}/login` by default. The redirect is skipped when the caller passes `rejectAuthFailure`, which the session fetch does. (`openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-api/src/openmrs-fetch.ts:225-243`, `openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-api/src/config-schema.ts:3`)
- Other failures keep an already-loaded session. If nothing has loaded yet, the error is recorded with `loaded: false`, and `initializing` is set during backend start-up. (`openmrs-esm-core/packages/framework/esm-api/src/current-user.ts:642-656`, `:593-599`)

**Caveat:** I read the store's promise logic in the hook, but I did not trace what the app shell renders in that error state. Based on the code, a component that calls `useSession()` before a session has loaded will not resolve while the store is in the error state. The app shell is the one that shows the error page, as the code comment says. I did not run the code.
